Fellow of the [[Academies of Belgium|Belgian Royal Academy of Medicine (ARMB)]] |website = {{url|https://wirtzlab.johnshopkins.edu/}} |spouse = }} '''Denis Wirtz''' is the vice provost for research and Theophilus Halley Smoot Professor of Engineering Science at [[Johns Hopkins University]]. He is an expert in the [[Molecular mechanics|molecular]] and [[Biophysics|biophysical]] mechanisms of [[cell migration|cell motility]] and [[Cell adhesion|adhesion]] and nuclear dynamics in health and disease.Keiger, Dale.[http://hub.jhu.edu/magazine/2013/winter/cancer-in-3d “Moving cancer research out of the Petri dish and into the third dimension”] ''Johns Hopkins Magazine'', Baltimore, 1 January 2013. Retrieved on 28 March 2016. Wirtz was the first to establish how a three-dimensional environment fundamentally affects the way cancer cells migrate, providing more biologically and medically relevant information than two-dimensional studies.{{cite web|title= Reddit Cancer AMA|date= 22 February 2016|url= https://www.reddit.com/r/science/comments/470lhl/science_ama_series_im_denis_wirtz_vice_provost/|access-date=2016-03-28}} He also pioneered the technique of particle-tracking [[microrheology]] to probe the [[rheological]] properties of complex fluids and living cells and tissues. He is a professor in the Departments of Chemical Engineering & Biomolecular Engineering and Materials Science & Engineering in the [[Whiting School of Engineering]], and in the Departments of Oncology and Pathology in the [[Johns Hopkins School of Medicine]].{{cite web|title=Denis Wirtz Profile Page|url=http://web.jhu.edu/administration/provost/bios/wirtz|access-date=2016-03-28}} Wirtz was named vice provost for research in February 2014, charged with directing the university's $2.24 billion research enterprise,O’Shea, Dennis [http://hub.jhu.edu/2015/12/09/research-funding-leader-nsf-survey “Johns Hopkins leads U.S. in research spending for 36th year in a row”], ''JHU Hub'', Baltimore, 9 December 2015. Retrieved on 1 March 2015. ==Biography== Wirtz was born in the [[Ixelles]] municipality of [[Brussels]], Belgium. He is fluent in English and French, and became a U.S. citizen in 2007. Wirtz earned a physics engineering degree at the [[Ecole Polytechnique]] of the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] in 1988. With a Hoover Fellowship from the [[Belgian American Educational Foundation]] (BAEF),{{Cite web|title= BAEF Fellowships: Alumni 1980–1989|url= http://www.baef.be/documents/alumni/alumni-1980-1989.xml?lang=en|access-date=2016-03-28}} he earned an M.S. and [[Doctorate|Ph.D]] in [[Chemical Engineering]] from [[Stanford University]], working in [[polymer physics]]. He was then granted a fellowship through the [[European Union]]’s Human Capital and Mobility program to conduct postdoctoral research at the [[ESPCI ParisTech|Ecole Supérieure de Physique et Chimie Industrielles (ESPCI)]] in Paris, France.{{cite web|title= Distinguished Lecturer – Denis Wirtz |url=http://www.cntc.uky.edu/2011/09/16/distiguished-lecturer-denis-wirtz/|access-date=2016-03-28}} Wirtz joined the faculty of the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at Johns Hopkins University in 1994 and was promoted to the rank of full professor in 2003. In 2009, he was selected to be the Theophilus Halley Smoot Professor of Engineering Science{{cite web|title= Chemical and biomolecular engineer Denis Wirtz named Smoot professor|url= http://www.nanowerk.com/news/newsid=14184.php|access-date=2016-03-28}} with secondary appointments in the departments of Materials Science and Engineering,{{cite web|title= Materials Science & Engineering: Associated Faculty|url= http://engineering.jhu.edu/materials/people/associated-faculty/|access-date=2016-03-28}} Pathology and Oncology, where he collaborates with fellow researchers in the [[Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center]].{{cite web|title= Faculty: Denis Wirtz|url= http://engineering.jhu.edu/chembe/faculty/denis-wirtz/|access-date=2016-03-28}}{{cite web|title=The Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center: Laboratory Scientists|url=http://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/kimmel_cancer_center/experts/Laboratory_Scientists/index3.html|access-date=2016-03-28}} Upon his appointment as the Theophilius Halley Smoot Professor of Engineering Physics,{{cite web|title= Chemical and biomolecular engineer Denis Wirtz named Smoot professor|url= http://www.nanowerk.com/news/newsid=14184.php|access-date=2016-03-28}}{{cite web|title=Theophilus Halley Smoot Professorship in Engineering: Established in 1981 by the estate of Theophilus H. Smoot|url=https://webapps.jhu.edu/namedprofessorships/professorshipdetail.cfm?professorshipID=99}} Dr. Nicholas Jones, former dean of the [[Whiting School of Engineering]], stated
"Throughout his time at Johns Hopkins, Denis has distinguished himself as an outstanding scholar and teacher. Additionally, Denis’ role as a catalyst for interdisciplinary research and collaboration at the university has proven extremely effective, both in terms of the research he conducts and the support he has attracted over the years. I am confident that his current research into the physical basis for cell adhesion and de-adhesion will prove critical to our understanding of the metastasis of [[cancer]] and enable important breakthroughs in the diagnosis and treatment of cancer in the years to come."{{cite web|title= Chemical and biomolecular engineer Denis Wirtz named Smoot professor|url= http://inbt.jhu.edu/2009/12/28/chemical-and-biomolecular-engineer-denis-wirtz-named-smoot-professor/|access-date=2016-03-28}}
In February 2014, Wirtz was named the vice provost for research at Johns Hopkins . In announcing the Wirtz's appointment, Provost [[Robert C. Lieberman]] stated,
"As is obvious to all who know him, Denis is an extremely productive and accomplished faculty member and a wonderful colleague. Those traits will serve both Denis and the university as he works with me to support important multidisciplinary research projects, including the strategic initiatives identified in the campaign, the Bloomberg Distinguished Professorships, and multidivisional proposals in response to RFAs (requests for applications)."{{cite web|title=Denis Wirtz named vice provost for research|url= http://hub.jhu.edu/gazette/2014/march-april/denis-wirtz-vice-provost-for-research|date= 2014-03-06}}
=== Vice provost === In his role as vice provost for research, Wirtz has recruited nearly two dozen faculty to join Johns Hopkins University as [[Bloomberg Distinguished Professorships|Bloomberg Distinguished Professors]],{{cite web|title=Bloomberg Distinguished Professorships|url= http://web.jhu.edu/administration/provost/BDP}} managed the inaugural year of the Catalyst and Discovery Awards,{{cite web|title= Wirtz relishes new role as vice provost for research|url=http://engineering.jhu.edu/chembe/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/2015/10/JHU-ChemBE-Bond_9.15_19.pdf|access-date=2016-03-25}}Hub Staff [http://hub.jhu.edu/at-work/2015/07/06/discovery-award-winners “Johns Hopkins Discovery Awards given to 23 cross-divisional research teams”], ''JHU Hub'', Baltimore, 6 July 2015. Retrieved on 25 March 2016.Hub Staff [http://hub.jhu.edu/at-work/2015/06/25/catalyst-award-winners “Catalyst Awards granted to 37 early-career Johns Hopkins researchers”], ''JHU Hub'', Baltimore, 25 June 2015. Retrieved on 25 March 2016. and the first two President's Frontier Awards.{{cite web|title=Johns Hopkins biologist Scott Bailey receives $250,000 President's Frontier Award|url=http://hub.jhu.edu/2016/02/01/frontier-award-scott-bailey|date=February 2016}} He has expanded the university's research development efforts, creating a weekly digest of limited submission opportunities,{{cite web|title=Limited Submissions at Johns Hopkins University|url= http://web.jhu.edu/administration/provost/awards/Limited_Submissions/About|access-date=2016-03-30}} a list of more than 175 funding opportunities for postdoctoral researchers,{{cite web|title= Post-doctoral Funding Opportunities|url=http://web.jhu.edu/administration/provost/awards/Postdoctoral_Funding|access-date=2016-03-30}} a list of more than 330 funding opportunities for early career faculty,{{cite web|title=Early Career Funding Opportunities|url= http://web.jhu.edu/administration/provost/awards/Early_Career|access-date=2016-03-30}} and consolidated monthly digests of internal funding opportunities at the institution.{{cite web|title= Internal Funding Opportunities|url= http://web.jhu.edu/administration/provost/awards/Internal|access-date=2016-03-30}} He also consolidated multiple research administration offices into a central research administration team, Johns Hopkins University Research Administration.{{cite web|title=Johns Hopkins University Research Administration|url= http://web.jhu.edu/administration/provost/programs_services/research/JHURA|access-date=2016-03-30}} As director of the university's Signature Initiatives, he has overseen the launch of two new signature initiatives on [[big data]], led by [[Alex Szalay]],{{cite web|title=Institute of Data Intensive Engineering and Science (IDIES)|url= http://idies.jhu.edu/|access-date=2016-03-30}} and space studies, Space@Hopkins, led by [[Charles L. Bennett]].{{cite web|title=JHU's Charles Bennett and Andrew Feinberg named Bloomberg Distinguished Professors|url= http://hub.jhu.edu/2015/12/15/bloomberg-distinguished-professors-bennett-and-feinberg|access-date=2016-03-30|date= 2015-12-15}} These are in addition to [[Kathryn Edin]]’s 21st Century Cities Initiative, [[Barbara Landau]]’s Science of Learning Institute, Scott Zeger’s Individualized Health Initiative, and David Peters’ Global Health Signature Initiative.{{cite web|title=Signature Initiatives|url= http://web.jhu.edu/administration/provost/initiatives/SI/index.html|access-date=2016-03-30}} Wirtz also directs the Johns Hopkins Physical Sciences-Oncology Center (PSOC),Gebel, Erika [http://engineering.jhu.edu/chembe/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/2013/11/chembe-fall09.pdf “Engineers Join Fight Against Cancer”] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701013514/http://engineering.jhu.edu/chembe/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/2013/11/chembe-fall09.pdf |date=2015-07-01 }}, ''ChemBE BOND'', Baltimore, Fall 2009. Retrieved on 28 March 2016 which is part of a network of twelve centers in the United States funded by the [[National Institutes of Health]]’s [[National Cancer Institute]] to link the [[physical sciences]] with the [[oncology|study of cancer]].{{cite journal|url= https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201006/cell.cfm |title= Cell is Mechanical Device |first=Calla |last=Cofield |journal=APS News |volume=19 |number=6 |date=June 2010|access-date=27 March 2016}} When the center was established with a $14.8M grant in 2009, Wirtz stated,
"For too long, not enough room has been made for nonconventional and nonbiological concepts borrowed from modern physics and engineering to tackle this disease. It is time to bring to the table ideas grounded in chemical and biomolecular engineering principles to develop new therapies and diagnostic tools. [The [[National Cancer Institute]] has] given us major funding for a center to study all the steps in the metastatic cascade."Gebel, Erika [http://engineering.jhu.edu/chembe/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/2013/11/chembe-fall09.pdf “Engineers Join Fight Against Cancer”] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701013514/http://engineering.jhu.edu/chembe/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/2013/11/chembe-fall09.pdf |date=2015-07-01 }}, ''ChemBE BOND'', Baltimore, Fall 2009. Retrieved on 28 March 2016
The PSOC is part of the Johns Hopkins Institute for NanoBioTechnology (INBT), which Wirtz co-founded and acts as associate director. INBT was launched in 2006 to "promote multidisciplinary research at the interface of [[nanotechnology]] and [[medicine]]."Spiro, Mary [http://hub.jhu.edu/at-work/2015/11/20/inbt-gerecht-and-mao “Institute for NanoBioTechnology adds two to leadership team”], ''HUB at Work'', Baltimore, 20 November 2010. Retrieved on 28 March 2016. With more than 250 affiliated faculty members from the Johns Hopkins [[Whiting School of Engineering|schools of Engineering]], [[Zanvyl Krieger School of Arts and Sciences|Arts and Sciences]], [[Johns Hopkins School of Medicine|Medicine]], and [[Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health|Public Health]] and scientists from the [[Applied Physics Laboratory]], the institute is home to several center grants and numerous education, training, and outreach programs. INBT counts [[Becton Dickinson]], [[MedImmune]], [[Northrop Grumman]], Secant Medical, and [[Under Armour]] among its corporate partners, and Wirtz has previously served as a Nikon Partner in Science since 2008.{{cite web|title=INBT Corporate Partnerships Program|url= http://inbt.jhu.edu/partnership/|access-date=2016-03-28}} Wirtz is the PI of a [[National Science Foundation]] Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) site in the Nanotechnology for Biology and Bioengineering program.{{cite web|title=Award Abstract #1460716: REU Site: Program in Nanotechnology for Biology and Bioengineering|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1460716 |access-date=2016-03-28}}{{cite web|title=National Science Foundation REU Sites |url=https://www.nsf.gov/crssprgm/reu/list_result.jsp?unitid=5048|access-date=2016-03-28}} Wirtz also founded the Johns Hopkins Center for Digital Pathology that brings together [[pathologists]], surgeons, [[oncologists]], and engineers to develop new single-cell technology for improved [[Diagnostic test|diagnostic]], [[Prognostics|prognostic]], therapeutic approaches for [[Disease|human diseases]], including [[cancer]], Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and [[Frailty syndrome|frailty in aging]].{{cite web|title=Center for Digital Pathology|url=http://digitalpathology.inbt.jhu.edu/|access-date=2016-03-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403230012/http://digitalpathology.inbt.jhu.edu/|archive-date=2016-04-03|url-status=dead}} He co-directs the Cancer Nanotechnology Training Center,{{cite web|title= Cancer Nanotechnology Training Centers (CNTCs)|url= http://nano.cancer.gov/action/programs/cntc.asp|access-date=2016-03-28}} another [[National Cancer Institute]]-funded entity. From 2005 to 2012, he also directed a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] (HHMI) funded interdisciplinary graduate research training program in [[nanotechnology]] for biology and [[medicine]]. The program aimed to produce researchers able to create new particles and materials to be used in the detection, treatment, prevention, and cure of [[Disease|human disease]]. It recruited students from [[biochemistry]], chemistry, physics, biology, and [[engineering]], while making a special effort to include minorities under-represented in science.{{cite web|title= HHMI Awards $10 Million for Interdisciplinary Graduate Education|url= http://www.hhmi.org/news/hhmi-awards-10-million-interdisciplinary-graduate-education|access-date=2016-03-26}} === Awards and distinctions === Wirtz was elected fellow of the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]] in 2006 for "major contributions in molecular cell mechanics and the development of particle tracking methods for cell and molecular biology."{{Cite web|title= Denis Wirtz, Ph.D. AIMBE College of Fellows Class of 2006|url=http://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/COF-1089/|access-date=2016-03-25}} In 2009, he was elected fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2009 "for contributions to cell micromechanics and cell adhesion and for the development and application of particle tracking methods to probe the micromechanical properties of living cells in normal conditions and disease state."Parsons, Tim [http://www.jhsph.edu/news/stories/2009/aaas-fellows-2009.html “Seven Johns Hopkins Researchers Named AAAS Fellows”], ''[[Johns Hopkins School of Public Health]]'', Baltimore, 19 December 2009. Retrieved on 25 March 2016.Spiro, Mary [http://inbt.jhu.edu/2009/12/21/inbt-eoc-directors-named-aaas-2009-fellows/ “INBT, EOC directors named AAAS 2009 Fellows”], ''Institute for NanoBioTechnology'', Baltimore, 21 December 2009. Retrieved on 25 March 2016. Wirtz was elected fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2010 for "his seminal contributions to the understanding of basic cellular functions through the development and application of novel biophysical methods grounded in statistical mechanics and polymer physics."American Physical Society [http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?institution=Johns%20Hopkins%20University&nom_unit=&year= “APS Fellow Archive”], [[American Physical Society]], Washington DC, 31 December 2010. The team invented a Cell Sensor Based Pathogen Detection that will enable “selective pathogran detection by exploiting the signalizing machinery of living cells.{{cite web|title=Faculty & Students Win Invention, Business Plan Awards|url= http://www.learningace.com/doc/5236630/8e8bfbbe3a97fad59c1b041dea0ba5a9/metrics-f05|access-date= 2016-03-28}} Since 2008, he has been the Editor-in-Chief of ''Cell Health and the Cytoskeleton''.{{cite web|title=Cell Health and Cytoskeleton, Editor-in-Chief: Professor Denis Wirtz|url=https://www.dovepress.com/cell-health-and-cytoskeleton-journal|access-date=2016-03-28}} He is on the Editorial Boards of ''[[Scientific Reports]]'', ''Cell Adhesion & Migration'',{{cite web|title= Cell Adhesion & Migration: Editorial Board|url= http://www.tandfonline.com/action/journalInformation?show=editorialBoard&journalCode=kcam20#.VvlskPlVikk|access-date=2016-03-28}} ''World Journal of Biological Chemistry'',{{cite web|title=World Journal of Biological Chemistry: Members of the Editorial Board|url=http://www.wjgnet.com/1949-8454/edboard.htm|access-date=2016-03-28|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218114142/http://www.wjgnet.com/1949-8454/edboard.htm|archive-date=2015-12-18}} and ''TECHNOLOGY''.{{cite web|title=TECHNOLOGY: Editorial Board|url=http://www.technologythejournal.com/board.html|access-date=2016-03-28}} Wirtz formerly served on the editorial boards of ''[[Physical Biology]]'', ''Journal of the Royal Society Interface Focus'', ''[[Biophysical Journal]]'',Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering [http://engineering.jhu.edu/chembe/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/2013/11/chembe-fall09.pdf “Faculty Awards”] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701013514/http://engineering.jhu.edu/chembe/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/2013/11/chembe-fall09.pdf |date=2015-07-01 }}, ''ChemBE BOND'', Baltimore, Fall 2009. |url=http://www.armb.be/index.php?id=6805|access-date=2020-05-05}} ==Research== Bridging the fields of chemical engineering, oncology, pathology, biophysics, and materials science, Wirtz's research focuses on the biophysical properties of healthy and diseased cells, including interactions between adjacent cells and the role of [[cellular architecture]] on nuclear shape and [[gene expression]].{{cite web|title=Faculty: Denis Wirtz|url= http://engineering.jhu.edu/chembe/faculty/denis-wirtz/|access-date=2016-03-30}} His research interests include cell biophysics, aging, tumor microenvironment, digital pathology, the actin cap, single molecule manipulation, intracellular particle trafficking, instrument development, tissue engineering, and nanotechnology in biology and Denis Wirtz is the vice provost for research and Theophilus Halley Smoot Professor of Engineering Science at Johns Hopkins University. He is an expert in the molecular and biophysical mechanisms of cell motility and adhesion and nuclear dynamics in health and disease.
Wirtz was the first to establish how a three-dimensional environment fundamentally affects the way cancer cells migrate, providing more biologically and medically relevant information than two-dimensional studies. He also pioneered the technique of particle-tracking microrheology to probe the rheological properties of complex fluids and living cells and tissues. He is a professor in the Departments of Chemical Engineering & Biomolecular Engineering and Materials Science & Engineering in the Whiting School of Engineering, and in the Departments of Oncology and Pathology in the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine.
Wirtz was named vice provost for research in February 2014, charged with directing the university's $2.24 billion research enterprise, implementing institutional research compliance, expanding research development, and producing and managing cross-divisional research initiatives, such as the Johns Hopkins Catalyst and Discovery Awards program, the President's Frontier Award program, and the Bloomberg Distinguished Professorships, which were established as part of a $350 million gift by Michael Bloomberg.
